description: Synthetic, fixed engineering and product-document retrieval judgments. Grades are 2 = directly answers the query, 1 = useful partial context, and 0 = lexical hard negative or irrelevant.

queries.query: How should a tenant-scoped database query filter organization data?

candidates.text: Tenant queries select records with organizationId and userId. Do not combine an organization arm and a personal arm with OR.
resolveOrganizationId verifies a caller belongs to the selected organization before a request continues.
The tenant onboarding form asks for an organization display name and an optional logo.
The release job packages the web application after unit tests finish.

queries.query: Can an invited project guest edit a project document?

candidates.text: Use canEditProject for project writes. Organization membership alone does not grant an invited guest permission to edit.
hasProjectAccess determines whether a caller may read a project, including invited project guests.
Guests can change their profile picture from the account settings page.
Document chunks are embedded before they are sent to the vector store.

queries.query: What is required when adding a tenant-aware Prisma table?

candidates.text: Edit schema.prisma, create and inspect a focused migration, regenerate clients, and add RLS policies for the tenant-aware table.
Use additive expand-contract migrations when a production deployment must remain compatible.
The Prisma dashboard lists database tables and migration timestamps for administrators.
The design system exposes a table component with striped row variants.

queries.query: Where should a Temporal workflow perform network I/O and time reads?

candidates.text: Keep workflows deterministic. Put network I/O, clocks, random values, and environment reads in activities, and make activities idempotent for retries.
Workflow control-flow changes require replay validation against representative histories.
The workflow page displays the most recent activity duration and retry count.
Temporal workers are deployed with a health endpoint for container probes.

queries.query: Must a wildcard API key still check the creator's current permission?

candidates.text: Yes. Every API-key request checks both the key scope and the creator's current permission, including a wildcard star scope.
Return distinguishable errors for an API key scope failure and a live permission failure.
A wildcard search query matches API keys whose display name contains the supplied words.
The UI copies an API key only once when it is created.

queries.query: What accessibility behavior is required for a modal confirmation dialog?

candidates.text: A modal dialog needs an accessible name, initial focus, keyboard focus trapping, and focus returned to the triggering control when it closes.
Destructive confirmation buttons use clear action labels instead of a vague affirmative label.
The dialog component accepts a modal prop that changes its drop shadow and width.
Product settings appear in the navigation sidebar after the project list.

queries.query: When does a production-shipping Fabric change need a changeset?

candidates.text: A user-visible or production-shipping behavior change needs a non-empty changeset, normally a fabric-app patch release.
Docs-only and CI-only changes can be skip-changeset eligible when the reason is recorded on the pull request.
A changeset is a short summary shown in the pull request file list.
DCO sign-off is added to commits with the git commit -s option.

queries.query: Why should RAG retrieval rerank a diversified candidate set?

candidates.text: Diversification removes near-duplicate contexts before reranking; the reranker then orders the distinct candidates by relevance and returns the configured top K.
An inline answering path may opt out of reranking when it cannot afford the extra model call.
Reranking the project dashboard changes the visual order of recent retrieval charts.
Chunk text is capped before embedding to keep vector generation within model limits.

queries.query: Can audit metadata include an API token if a redactor runs later?

candidates.text: No. Audit metadata and resource names must never contain credentials. The sensitive-key redactor is defense in depth, not permission to pass secrets.
Security-relevant mutations should emit the appropriate audit action, often through recordAuditFromRequest.
The audit log supports filtering by an API action name and by date range.
Tokens are counted before an AI prompt is submitted to a model provider.

queries.query: What must be checked when changing the MCP server management dialog?

candidates.text: Inspect and test both intentionally paired MCP management dialogs: the primary servers view and the settings configuration dialog.
When a navigation surface changes, update the Get Started registry, tour steps, anchors, and translation copy together.
The MCP server dialog uses a two-column layout for environment variable names and values.
MCP clients use a gateway to read tool definitions from configured servers.

queries.query: How are Fabric pull requests landed after checks pass?

candidates.text: Fabric pull requests land through the OSS relay. Authorize the exact head SHA with /relay and apply ready-for-relay; do not use gh pr merge.
A push makes an earlier relay authorization stale, so the exact current head needs a new relay comment.
The relay status panel displays pull request labels next to the branch name.
The changelog is generated from released package versions.

queries.query: What should retrieval do if the reranker service cannot score candidates?

candidates.text: If reranking fails, return the original diversified retrieval order so a reranker outage does not prevent context delivery.
Reranking is skipped when there is at most one candidate because it cannot change the result order.
The reranker failure banner is shown at the top of the retrieval settings page.
The vector store client retries a transient collection creation request.
